cards.text: Haggai, a prophet of the LORD, already heard from Him on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month (Hag 2:10). Now the word of the LORD comes to Haggai AGAIN. Friend, some days I get one message and I need to go lie down on my gold base.

cards.question: This new word of the LORD comes to Haggai on that very same day, the twenty-fourth day of the month.

cards.text: This one's for Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, and Haggai's the delivery guy. Friend, this package is HEAVY.

cards.question: In His message for Zerubbabel, what does the LORD say He's about to shake?

cards.text: Then the LORD gets specific about the nations. If you're sitting on a throne right now, friend, I'd sit VERY carefully.

cards.question: In His message for Zerubbabel, the LORD says He will protect the royal thrones of the nations.
The LORD says He'll overturn royal thrones. What else does He say He'll destroy among the nations?

cards.text: Then the LORD turns to the battlefield: He'll overturn chariots and their riders. Flipped like cookies off a spatula, and THOSE never land pretty.

cards.question: With the chariots overturned, how does the LORD say the horses and their riders will fall?

answers.text: Each by the sword of his brother
Each by a stone from a sling
Each under the waves of the sea

cards.text: Thrones flipping, chariots flipping, and then the LORD calls one man by name, his father's name too. "On that day," He says, He will take Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel.

cards.question: Zerubbabel is governor of Judah, but the LORD gives him another title. He calls Zerubbabel "My ___."
On that day, what does the LORD say He will make His servant Zerubbabel like?
The LORD tells Zerubbabel why He'll make him like His signet ring: "for I have ___ you."

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 13 quotes "for I have ___ you.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The throne joke ('If you're sitting on a throne right now, friend, I'd sit VERY carefully') tells the baker that thrones are in danger. That gives away card 6, which asks whether the LORD will protect the royal thrones (False). It also rules out the True answer before the baker picks.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Card 1 gives the date of the earlier word (the twenty-fourth day, Hag 2:10) and then says the word comes AGAIN. The joke then frames it as a same-day pileup ('some days I get one message'). Together these all but answer card 2, which asks whether the new word came on that same day, the twenty-fourth.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
